agree.reason: The finished art, the signed quote and the clear budget would reassure this wary backer, but there is no refund promise, no update schedule and no risks section, so a reader who has already lost $85 to a first-time creator still has little protection.

honest.reason: It drops the 'proven hit' claim and admits 23 ratings is a small sample, but it calls the convention players 'strangers' who played it 'cold' without saying most of the 23 ratings came from people at the designer's own table, and it treats email sign-ups as people waiting to buy.

works_the_facts.reason: The budget table works correctly from the brief: about 570 backers, ~$2,800 in fees, ~$5,150 shipping and ~$2,650 left over; it doesn't say what the leftover covers or what the 930 extra copies are for.

right_comparison.reason: The only comparison is a generic one, 'most crowdfunding games are promises'; it never weighs the reader's real choices, such as waiting for retail or what happens to their money if the project slips.

qualification.reason: The only hedge is 'if that date changes, I'll tell you', which the reader can't check; the writer left out the available promise of a full refund if delivery is more than three months past November and the update every two weeks.

objections.reason: It answers the first-timer worry with finished assets, a signed quote and a full-time-job schedule, but it omits the facts that would answer it best: the refund promise, the update schedule and the reviewer's video in launch week.

fit.reason: It is a roughly 500-word campaign pitch with sensible sections, but the title is left as a '[Game Title]' placeholder even though the name, Lantern Winter, was known.
